title: Inorder Successor/Predecessor in BST
problemStatement: Solve “Inorder Successor/Predecessor in BST” as posed in the A2Z sheet (Practice Problems).
intuition: "Inorder Successor/Predecessor in BST" lives in binary search. Define a monotonic predicate P(mid). Search the answer space or the index space; keep the invariant that the answer still lies in [lo, hi].

approaches.title: Brute: linear scan
approaches.idea: Scan every candidate until the condition holds.

approaches.title: Optimal: binary search on monotonic predicate
approaches.idea: Shrink [lo, hi] using mid; be consistent about inclusive bounds.
approaches.time: O(log n) on array search; O(f·log A) on answer-space search
approaches.dryRun: Maintain: answer ∈ [lo, hi). Each step halves the interval.
approaches.whyWorks: Monotonicity guarantees one side can be discarded safely.

complexity.time: O(log n) on array search; O(f·log A) on answer-space search

commonMistakes: Infinite loop from wrong mid update
Off-by-one on lower vs upper bound
Using binary search without a proven monotonic predicate
patternRecognition: Minimize/maximize a value with a yes/no check → binary search on answer
followUps: Binary search on answer — write the feasibility check
interviewInsight: Say the invariant out loud for "Inorder Successor/Predecessor in BST". Strong candidates never hand-wave lo/hi updates.
